clue.text: Shape metal as the Rubicon crossed?

definitions.meaning: to form metal by pouring it molten into a mould
Julius Caesar is said to have declared 'the die is cast' as he crossed the Rubicon, committing himself to civil war

explanation.surface: A puzzling question pairing metalwork with Caesar's fateful river crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into DIE CAST, Caesar's 'alea iacta est', spoken as he crossed the Rubicon into Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Casting metal in a mould (a die) is the foundry process this compound adjective and verb names.

clue.text: Terrible killer, an idiot

definitions.meaning: an expanding bullet that causes dreadful wounds

explanation.surface: A dreadful murderer turns out to be a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: The bullet takes its name from Dum Dum arsenal in India; the slang sense doubles dumb.

clue.text: Too much for two characters, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the two letters are spoken by their names rather than written

parts.note: the two letters X and S, read by their names

explanation.surface: Wondering whether two letters are more than enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' looks like people, but they are letters: X and S spoken as their names, 'ex' and 'ess'.
explanation.definitionFit: Excess means an amount beyond what is needed or permitted, more than enough.

clue.text: Old lady of Turin turns up with car after arrival of the Messiah

indicators.note: turns up in a down clue means these pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: donna is Italian for lady, and Turin is in Italy
the Mini is a classic small British car

explanation.surface: An elderly Italian woman arrives by car after the Second Coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns up' reverses the old lady because this is a down clue, read from the bottom; 'of Turin' tells you to use the Italian word.
explanation.definitionFit: Anno Domini, in the year of our Lord, labels the years counted after the birth of Christ.

clue.text: Stale when married? That's about right

indicators.note: about means the word for when married goes round the letter for right

parts.note: a couple who are married have tied the knot, so are tied

explanation.surface: A cynical remark that marriage makes things go flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's about' tells you the married word wraps round the letter for right.
explanation.definitionFit: A tired joke or idea is stale, worn out by overuse.

clue.text: Lithuanian capital providing dandy start to long journey

indicators.note: capital here means the capital letter, the first letter at the head of the word Lithuanian

parts.note: providing, as in 'on condition that', means if
a toff is a smartly dressed upper-class man, a dandy

explanation.surface: Vilnius as the departure point for a fashionable traveller's long trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lithuanian capital' looks like Vilnius, but it is only the capital letter of Lithuanian.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket's launch is the moment of leaving the ground, the opening of a long voyage into space.

clue.text: Foreign fliers beginning to fly at heads of untold falcons, flew madly

indicators.note: madly means the collected letters fly around in wild disorder
beginning to means just the first letter of fly is taken
heads of means the first letters of untold and falcons

explanation.surface: A wild scene of falcons swooping madly through the air.
explanation.walkthrough: F, AT, U, F and FLEW are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Luftwaffe is the German air force, so its pilots are airmen from abroad.

clue.text: Weary signal

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to droop with tiredness, and the cloth waved to send a message.

clue.text: Meat giving one gout unfortunately, if unknown amount's consumed

indicators.note: consumed means swallowed up, so the letter for an unknown goes inside the jumbled letters
unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters of one gout are mixed up

parts.note: x is the standard algebra symbol for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A rich meat that brings on gout if you eat too much.
explanation.walkthrough: OTONGUE, the anagram of ONE GOUT, takes X after its first O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ox tongue is beef tongue, a cut of offal cooked and served as cold meat.

clue.text: Japanese vessel may be heading to Newcastle, abandoned

parts.note: a Japanese cup or flask may be meant for sake, the rice wine

indicators.note: heading to means just the first letter of Newcastle

explanation.surface: A Japanese ship bound for Newcastle has been deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a container: one may be FOR SAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsaken means deserted or left behind, the same as abandoned.

clue.text: Wine staying dry then?

definitions.meaning: a red or white Burgundy from the town of ...
wearing a mac, a raincoat, keeps you dry

explanation.surface: A wine that somehow keeps you dry, a teetotal joke.
explanation.walkthrough: MAC is short for mackintosh, a British word for a raincoat; with your mac on you stay dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Macon is a Burgundy appellation from the area around the French town of that name.

clue.text: Telescope seeing far on the periphery in nuclear device

indicators.note: in tells us the edge letters of far are placed inside the word for the nuclear device

parts.note: a reactor is a device for nuclear fission

indicators.note: on the periphery means only the outermost letters of far are used

explanation.surface: Looking far out with a telescope placed inside a nuclear plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters of 'far', F and R, go into REACTOR after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A refractor is a kind of telescope that gathers light through lenses rather than mirrors.

clue.text: Winning team losing? That's muddled

parts.note: a team ahead in a match is up
a side is a team
a team behind in a match is down

explanation.surface: A sports fan baffled that a team can be both winning and losing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something turned upside down is in total disorder, thoroughly confused or jumbled.

clue.text: Old South American driving endlessly?

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the phrase for driving is cut off

parts.note: someone driving is in a car

explanation.surface: An elderly man from South America who never stops driving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driving' is IN CAR; 'endlessly' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas were the people of the pre-Columbian empire in the Andes, so one is an ancient South American.

clue.text: Sticking a blade nethermost — sliding around, is it?

definitions.text: Sticking a blade nethermost — sliding around, is it?

indicators.note: sliding around means the letters slip about into a new order
nethermost means lowest, so in a word written across it is the final letter of blade

explanation.surface: Describing a skater gliding on blades fixed underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: STICKINGA plus E, the last letter of blade, are rearranged; the whole clue also describes the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Skaters glide over ice on blades fixed beneath their boots, sliding about.

clue.text: Make the truth available to all, probing organic waste

indicators.note: probing means pushing into, so these pieces go inside the word for organic waste

parts.note: manure is dung used as fertiliser
a fact is the truth
U is the British film certificate for universal, suitable for all audiences

explanation.surface: An investigative reporter digging the truth out of a dung heap for public view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Probing' puts the truth and the universal letter inside the waste. U is the British film rating meaning anyone may watch.
explanation.definitionFit: To manufacture is to produce goods, a synonym of the verb to make.

clue.text: Ornate enamel apt for sign

indicators.note: ornate means elaborately decorated, so the letters are rearranged into a new design

explanation.surface: Decorative enamel work suitable for a shop sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A nameplate is a plaque on a door or wall showing a name, a kind of sign.

clue.text: Back Duke Ellington for a start, on guitar

indicators.note: for a start means only the opening letter of Ellington

parts.note: Fender is a famous make of electric guitar

explanation.surface: Duke Ellington beginning a number on guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duke Ellington' is the jazz bandleader, but split: D for duke, E from Ellington.
explanation.definitionFit: In football and similar games, a back is a defensive player.

clue.text: Emotional disorder ending in Britain with relative in Brussels?

indicators.note: ending in means the last letter of Britain

parts.note: a sister, SIS, who is European, a Euro-sis, seated in Brussels with the EU

explanation.surface: An anxious Briton whose relative lives in Brussels.
explanation.walkthrough: N, the end of Britain, then EURO-SIS: a sister given the Brussels label EURO.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurosis is a mental condition marked by anxiety, obsession or depression.

clue.text: All left-hand pages are still to go on book

parts.note: even, as in 'even more', means still
Numbers is the fourth book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A remark about books: the left-hand pages remain to be dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To go on' merely joins the two pieces. The definition completes a statement about how books are paginated.
explanation.definitionFit: In a printed book page one is a right-hand page, so the left-hand pages carry 2, 4, 6 and so on.

clue.text: Neglect a line in book of prayer

parts.note: to miss something is to neglect or overlook it

explanation.surface: Skipping a line while reading from a prayer book.
explanation.definitionFit: A missal is the book containing the texts used in celebrating Mass through the year.

clue.text: Note of course, heard

indicators.note: heard means the word for course is spoken and we write what it sounds like

parts.note: tenor means the general course or drift of something, as in the tenor of a debate

explanation.surface: A musical note that one naturally hears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks musical, and 'course' hints at a meal, but a tenner is a banknote: a British ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenner is informal British slang for a ten-pound banknote.

clue.text: Noble almost abandoning extremes

indicators.note: abandoning extremes means the word for almost loses its first and last letters

parts.note: nearly means almost

explanation.surface: An aristocrat who nearly gives up radical politics.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman ranking above a viscount and below a marquess.

clue.text: Train in a particular area requiring less pace, one twice derailed

indicators.note: derailed suggests a train thrown off its track, so the letters are thrown into disorder
twice means the letter for one is used two times

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A railway story: a slower train, a carriage twice off the rails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like the railway, but it is the verb in the definition. The letters of LESS PACE plus I and I are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To specialise is to concentrate one's study or work in one narrow field.

clue.text: Seeing revolutionary monarch, shout "hooray"

parts.note: Che Guevara was the Argentine-born Marxist revolutionary
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher of the British queen

explanation.surface: Crowds cheering when they see a rebel leader and a king.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer is to shout in approval or encouragement, as with hooray.

clue.text: One's sat upon in non-U America, as an American might say?

indicators.note: non-U, the old class label for unrefined speech, here means without the letter U

parts.words: America, as an American might say
parts.note: an American may call the country the US of A

explanation.surface: Musing on what Americans, free of British class labels, call a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-U' recalls Nancy Mitford's U and non-U, upper-class versus other British usage, but just drops the U from US OF A.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa is a padded seat for several people, something you sit on.

clue.text: In time, malfunctioning coils put out of place

indicators.note: In at the start means the rearranged letters go inside the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: malfunctioning means not working properly, so the letters of coils are jumbled

explanation.surface: Coils on some machine failing and dislodging something in due course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' at the start places ISLOC, the anagram that 'malfunctioning' makes of coils, inside the word for time.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislocate a joint or object is to shift it from its proper position.

clue.text: Author elected to keep a tragedy in stock?

indicators.note: to keep means the word for elected holds the other piece inside

parts.note: a politician elected is in
BSE, mad cow disease, was a disaster for British livestock in the 1990s

explanation.surface: A writer voted in and stockpiling a tragic play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tragedy' looks theatrical, fitting the playwright, but 'stock' means livestock: BSE is bovine spongiform encephalopathy.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian dramatist who wrote A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: Pink bottom breaking eggs

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open the word for eggs to fit the other piece inside

parts.note: roe is the mass of eggs of a fish
seat is a polite word for the buttocks

explanation.surface: Someone sits on eggs and is left pink-faced with a sore behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Roseate means rose-coloured, a soft shade of pink.

clue.text: Hollow cut in back for uniform

indicators.note: in means the trimmed word for hollow goes inside the word for back

parts.note: the rear is the back

indicators.note: cut means the word for hollow has its tail letter chopped off

parts.note: a gulf is a deep hollow or chasm

explanation.surface: A gardener's instruction: cut a hollow into the back for an even finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' trims the hollow to GUL, and 'in' places that inside the word for back.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular means even and consistent, unchanging in pattern, as uniform does.
